financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (Bank standalone) basis. EPS 8.76 = 3,903,698k/~445.6mn weighted-average shares (period-end count 450,715,084; disclosed EPS implies weighted-average ~445,626,940, consistent with the scrip dividend issued during the period). See GROUP row's notes for shared subsidiary structure, the H1 2025 discontinued-operations one-off, and full extraction detail.

DFCC Bank PLC, a licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). This filing discloses full separate Bank AND consolidated Group columns in every primary statement (Income Statement p.7, Statement of Profit or Loss & OCI p.8, Statement of Financial Position p.9, Statement of Cash Flows p.12) -- entered as TWO rows: basis='GROUP' and basis='COMPANY' (Bank standalone). Per Note 3 (p.13), the Group comprises the Bank and subsidiaries DFCC Consulting (Pvt) Limited, Lanka Industrial Estates Limited and Synapsys Limited, plus associate National Asset Management Limited -- no insurance subsidiary remains in the current Group structure (consistent with this being a historical/divested interest; see the one-off discontinued-operations item below). This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) 'For the period ended' columns, not the quarter-only columns also present. Mapped per bank convention: revenue = 'Total operating income' (Bank 23,198,913; Group 23,657,800). operating_profit = DFCC's own pre-levy subtotal 'Operating profit before taxes on financial services' (Bank 7,600,056; Group 7,919,721). profit_before_tax = 'Profit before income tax' -- AFTER Taxes on financial services (Rs.2,120,554k, same both bases) and, for Group, after adding Share of profit of associate (Rs.1,767k) -- Bank 5,479,502; Group 5,800,934. tax_expense = 'Income tax expense' (Bank 1,575,804; Group 1,661,963). profit_after_tax = 'Profit for the period' -- the current period (H1 2026) has ZERO discontinued-operations profit at both Bank and Group level, so this equals 'Profit for the period from continuing operations' (Bank 3,903,698; Group 4,138,971, of which Rs.89,439k is non-controlling interest, stored in minority_interest; equity holders' share is Rs.4,049,532k). finance_costs/finance_income and current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables all omitted per bank convention. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks' (Bank 7,658,746; Group 7,658,746). long_term_borrowings = 'Due to other borrowers' + 'Debt securities issued' + 'Subordinated term debt' (Bank: 118,028,705+10,309,741+19,128,192=147,466,638; Group: 117,997,643+10,309,741+19,128,192=147,435,576). 'Due to depositors' (Bank 631,992,560; Group 630,908,446) is deliberately excluded per instructions. cash_and_equivalents = balance-sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' line only (Bank 20,606,492; Group 20,648,651) -- narrower than the cash-flow statement's own period-end reconciliation figure (Rs.37,668,238k Bank / Rs.37,710,397k Group), which DFCC defines as Cash and cash equivalents PLUS Placements with banks; the balance-sheet line is used for consistency with this project's standard field. total_assets/total_liabilities/total_equity per Statement of Financial Position p.9 -- Group total_equity stored INCLUDING non-controlling interests (Rs.110,019,493k, vs Rs.109,352,567k attributable to equity holders of the Bank alone) so that total_assets = total_liabilities + total_equity ties exactly. shares_in_issue = 450,715,084 (Note 14.2, 'Number of shares of the Bank' as at 30.06.2026 -- same count applies to both rows, since NCI is subsidiary-level equity, not Bank ordinary shares). EPS cross-check: this is a PERIOD-END count; DFCC issued a scrip dividend during H1 2026 (stated capital Rs.15,445,973k to Rs.17,388,007k; shares 438,404,250 at 31.12.2025 to 450,715,084 at 30.06.2026), so the weighted-average count used for EPS is lower than the period-end count. Implied weighted-average from disclosed EPS: Bank 3,903,698,000/8.76=445,626,940; Group (equity holders' share) 4,049,532,000/9.09=445,438,065 -- both consistent with each other and fall between the Dec-2025 and Jun-2026 share counts as expected, confirming no data-entry error. Cash flow figures per Statement of Cash Flows p.12: cash_from_operations = Bank 1,606,463 / Group 1,752,185 ('Net cash flows from/(used in) operating activities'); capex = Bank 970,530 / Group 1,191,956 ('Purchase of property, equipment, intangibles and investment property' -- the actual cash-flow-statement capex line; NOT the smaller Rs.660,132k Group 'Total capital expenditure' shown in the Operating Segments note on p.26, which only allocates capex to the 'Other Unallocated' segment column and is evidently a narrower/different-basis figure -- the cash flow statement figure is used as authoritative capex per project convention); cash_from_investing = Bank -8,399,814 / Group -8,621,240; cash_from_financing = Bank -15,752,414 / Group -15,668,414. MAJOR ONE-OFF FLAGGED IN THE PRIOR-YEAR COMPARATIVE (not in the current period): the H1 2025 comparative included 'Profit for the period from discontinued operations, net of tax' of Rs.4,967,916k at BANK/standalone level but only Rs.116,274k at GROUP/consolidated level (p.7) -- almost certainly a gain on disposal of an investment (recognised largely as a standalone-book gain at the Bank level, where the investment was carried at low historic cost, but substantially eliminated on consolidation at Group level, where the carrying value of the underlying net assets was already higher). H1 2026 has ZERO discontinued-operations profit at both levels. This materially distorts a naive Bank-basis YoY 'Profit for the period' comparison (apparent -62.9%, Rs.10,523,199k to Rs.3,903,698k); the CORE continuing-operations decline is much smaller: Bank -29.7% (Rs.5,555,283k to Rs.3,903,698k), Group -28.0% (Rs.5,746,646k to Rs.4,138,971k, continuing-ops basis). Management's own commentary (CEO's statement and Income Statement Analysis, pp.2-6) explicitly compares continuing-operations ('core operations') figures for both periods, avoiding this distortion -- this entry's note_text follows the same convention. Confirmation subtotals tie out exactly: Bank total assets 919,423,278 = total liabilities 810,921,474 + total equity 108,501,804. Group total assets 920,890,485 = total liabilities 810,870,992 + total equity(incl. NCI) 110,019,493. PBT - tax = PAT: Bank 5,479,502-1,575,804=3,903,698 (exact); Group 5,800,934-1,661,963=4,138,971 (exact, incl. NCI). Page numbers used: Income Statement p.7 (OCI statement p.8), Statement of Financial Position p.9, Statement of Cash Flows p.12, shareholder/shares-in-issue info p.16-17, CEO's statement pp.5-6, Income Statement Analysis narrative pp.2-4, Financial Position Analysis pp.4-5, Selected Performance Indicators (ratios) p.20.

interim_updates.note_text: DFCC Bank's H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) results show genuine core-business income growth against a much weaker profit line, driven mainly by deliberately higher impairment provisioning and cost growth, plus a large prior-year one-off that inflates the apparent YoY profit decline. Group Net Interest Income grew 6% to Rs.16,170,675k (from Rs.15,207,127k), supported by a 20% YoY expansion in the loan portfolio and a 17% expansion in the asset base, while Net Interest Margin held at 3.66% (down slightly from 3.96% at 31 Dec 2025). Group Net Fee and Commission Income grew 29% to Rs.4,186,837k (from Rs.3,248,861k), driven by credit-card portfolio expansion and trade-related commissions. Group Total Operating Income rose 5.6% to Rs.23,657,800k. Against this, Group Impairment Charges for loans and other losses rose 33% to Rs.4,630,200k (from Rs.3,482,374k) -- management explicitly attributes this to refinements of internal ECL models and new management overlays for higher-risk sectors and 'specific large group exposures', a deliberate strengthening of prudential buffers rather than deteriorating asset quality (the net Stage 3 impaired-loan ratio actually IMPROVED to 3.61% from 4.55% at 31 Dec 2025). Group Total Operating Expenses rose 31% to Rs.11,107,879k (from Rs.8,457,396k), driven by Personnel Expenses +42% (annual salary revisions and performance-based incentives) and continued investment in IT/digital transformation and marketing/brand initiatives. As a result, Group Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services fell 24% to Rs.7,919,721k (from Rs.10,479,667k), and Group PBT fell 29% to Rs.5,800,934k (from Rs.8,172,087k). Group Income Tax Expense fell 31% to Rs.1,661,963k (from Rs.2,425,441k), broadly proportionate to the PBT decline (not a distorting swing). Group Profit for the Period fell 29.4% to Rs.4,138,971k (from Rs.5,862,920k); however, this YoY comparison is itself mildly distorted by the H1 2025 comparative, which included Rs.116,274k of Group 'discontinued operations' profit (versus a much larger Rs.4,967,916k at the standalone Bank level, almost entirely eliminated on consolidation -- see NOTE for detail) -- on a strictly continuing-operations basis, Group PAT fell 28.0% (Rs.5,746,646k to Rs.4,138,971k), and Bank (standalone) PAT fell 29.7% (Rs.5,555,283k to Rs.3,903,698k), both materially smaller declines than the 62.9% headline drop a reader would see comparing Bank 'Profit for the period' totals naively (Rs.10,523,199k to Rs.3,903,698k) without adjusting for the one-off. Return on Equity fell to 6.19% from 11.55% at 31 Dec 2025 (a full-year reference point). Deposits grew 12% and loans 9% since 31 Dec 2025, with the CASA ratio improving to 24.99%; Total Capital Ratio was 15.746% (Group), comfortably above the 12.5% regulatory minimum.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the FIRST financial_statements entry for DFCC in this database (a prior documents-table reference to a 'period ended 30 September 2025' filing exists but was never entered into financial_statements and is superseded/stale -- ignored per instructions). Reporting basis: DFCC has a 31 December FYE and reports 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1) figures in this filing, alongside quarter-only columns not used here, consistent with other banks entered this session. Both GROUP and COMPANY (Bank standalone) rows were stored since this filing discloses both in full.
interim_updates.takeaway: Core banking income momentum is genuinely strong (Group NII +6% to Rs.16.17bn, Net Fee & Commission Income +29% to Rs.4.19bn, loan book +20% YoY), but Group PBT fell 29% and PAT fell 29.4% because management deliberately strengthened impairment provisioning (Group impairment charges +33% to Rs.4.63bn via ECL model refinements and overlays for specific large group exposures -- even as the net Stage 3 ratio improved to 3.61% from 4.55%) and personnel/opex costs rose 42%/31% on salary revisions and digital investment. A naive Bank-basis PAT comparison (down 62.9%) is exaggerated by a Rs.4.97bn one-off gain on disposal of an investment recognised at the standalone Bank level in H1 2025 (largely eliminated on consolidation, only Rs.116mn hit the Group P&L) -- on a continuing-operations basis, both Bank and Group PAT declines are closer to 28-30%, driven by the deliberate provisioning and cost decisions above rather than a deterioration in the underlying franchise.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Group Net Interest Income +6% YoY to Rs.16,170,675k (from Rs.15,207,127k), on 20% loan book growth and 17% asset base growth YoY; Net Interest Margin 3.66% (down from 3.96% at 31 Dec 2025)
Group Net Fee and Commission Income +29% YoY to Rs.4,186,837k (from Rs.3,248,861k), driven by credit-card portfolio expansion and trade-related commissions

Group Impairment Charges +33% YoY to Rs.4,630,200k (from Rs.3,482,374k) -- explicitly attributed to ECL model refinements and management overlays for higher-risk sectors and 'specific large group exposures', a deliberate prudential strengthening; net Stage 3 impaired-loan ratio nonetheless IMPROVED to 3.61% from 4.55% at 31 Dec 2025
Group Total Operating Expenses +31% YoY to Rs.11,107,879k, driven by Personnel Expenses +42% (salary revisions, performance incentives) and continued IT/digital and marketing investment

Group PBT -29% YoY to Rs.5,800,934k and Group PAT -29.4% YoY to Rs.4,138,971k; on a continuing-operations basis (stripping out a Rs.4.97bn one-off disposal gain recognised at Bank-standalone level in H1 2025), Group PAT decline is a smaller 28.0% and Bank PAT decline is 29.7%

Post-period-end (1 August 2026): Group completed acquisition of Standard Chartered Bank PLC's Wealth and Retail Banking business in Sri Lanka for Rs.4.4bn cash (~50,000 customer accounts, ~260 employees, network expanded to 139 locations) -- a non-adjusting subsequent event, not reflected in the 30 June 2026 balance sheet
key_drivers: Impairment charges +33% YoY (Rs.3,482,374k to Rs.4,630,200k, Group) is the single largest driver of the PBT decline -- management frames this as deliberate prudential strengthening (ECL model refinements, overlays for specific large group exposures) rather than credit deterioration, supported by the net Stage 3 ratio improving to 3.61% from 4.55%
Personnel expenses +42% YoY (annual salary revisions and performance-based incentive payments) drove most of the 31% rise in Group Total Operating Expenses to Rs.11,107,879k

A Rs.4,967,916k one-off gain on disposal of an investment, recognised almost entirely at the standalone Bank level in the H1 2025 comparative (only Rs.116,274k reached the Group P&L, eliminated on consolidation), inflates the apparent Bank-basis PAT decline to 62.9% when the underlying continuing-operations decline is 29.7% (Bank) / 28.0% (Group)

Core revenue growth (Net Interest Income +6%, Net Fee & Commission Income +29%, Group) reflects genuine business momentum -- loan book +20% YoY and CASA ratio improving to 24.99% -- and is not itself a source of the profit decline
